newsitem.title: FRANCE: France cuts farmers' water use over drought fears.
newsitem.headline: France cuts farmers' water use over drought fears.

text.p: The French government has ordered farmers in the Beauce, Europe's biggest grain producing region, to reduce irrigation of their crops due to early signs of drought, the Environment Ministry said on Monday.
Noel Godard, assistant director of water management at the ministry, said a rainfall deficit over the past year, worsened by sparse rain in March, had dried out lower soil levels.
"It's true that there have been the beginnings of a drought since March in certain regions because of a low rainfall. As of May...the situation will be clearer," Godard said.
The Beauce region, located between Paris's outer southern suburbs and the city of Orleans is considered the bread basket of France, Europe's largest grain producer.
It produces some five million tonnes of wheat per year, or one-sixth of France's wheat crop, as well as a million tonnes each of corn and barley.
Other areas showing signs of drought include upper Normandy, Nord-Pas-de-Calais and the Mediterranean coastal areas, but no water-saving measures have been introduced there.
However, ministry officials said restrictions on water use could be ordered soon in the Paris area.

Rapid early growth in crops caused by unusually warm weather in March prompted farmers in the Beauce, as well as in the western Poitou-Charentes region and the Drome area in the southeast, to begin irrigation earlier than usual.
